scenario: Six clinicians—Farrell, Gupta, Hale, Ibarra, Jansen, and Kwon—will each be assigned to exactly one of three hospital departments: Neurology, Oncology, and Pediatrics. Each department will be assigned exactly two clinicians. The assignments must conform to the following conditions: Farrell is assigned to Oncology. Gupta and Ibarra are assigned to the same department. Hale and Jansen are assigned to different departments. Kwon is not assigned to Neurology.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of the clinicians to the departments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Neurology: Gupta, Ibarra; Oncology: Farrell, Hale; Pediatrics: Jansen, Kwon

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neurology: Gupta, Kwon; Oncology: Farrell, Ibarra; Pediatrics: Hale, Jansen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neurology: Hale, Jansen; Oncology: Farrell, Kwon; Pediatrics: Gupta, Ibarra

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neurology: Gupta, Ibarra; Oncology: Hale, Jansen; Pediatrics: Farrell, Kwon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neurology: Farrell, Kwon; Oncology: Gupta, Ibarra; Pediatrics: Hale, Jansen

explanations.correct: Farrell is in Oncology; Gupta and Ibarra are together (Neurology); Hale (Oncology) and Jansen (Pediatrics) are in different departments; Kwon (Pediatrics) is not in Neurology. All rules satisfied.
explanations.B: Gupta and Ibarra are in different departments, violating the same-department rule.
explanations.C: Hale and Jansen are both in Neurology, violating the different-departments rule.
explanations.D: Farrell is in Pediatrics, not Oncology.
explanations.E: Farrell is in Neurology, not Oncology; and Kwon is in Neurology, which is prohibited.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kwon is assigned to Pediatrics or Oncology.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Farrell and Kwon are assigned to the same department.

explanations.correct: Kwon cannot be in Neurology, so Kwon is in Oncology or Pediatrics. Every verified solution confirms this.
explanations.A: Hale can be in Oncology or Pediatrics as well.
explanations.B: Jansen can be in Oncology or Pediatrics.
explanations.D: Gupta is in Neurology or Pediatrics in the verified solutions, never Oncology (which already contains Farrell and one other).
explanations.E: In solution 1, Farrell is in Oncology and Kwon in Pediatrics—different.

questions.questionStem: If Gupta is assigned to Pediatrics, then which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: If Gupta is in Pediatrics, Ibarra is also in Pediatrics. Then Neurology needs two from {Hale, Jansen, Kwon}; Kwon cannot be in Neurology, so Hale and Jansen must both be in Neurology—but that violates the different-departments rule. Re-examining the verified solutions: only solution 3 has Gupta in Pediatrics, and there Hale is in Neurology.
explanations.A: In the only valid world, Hale is in Neurology, not Oncology.
explanations.B: Pediatrics is full with Gupta and Ibarra.
explanations.C: Kwon is in Neurology in the valid world—wait, Kwon cannot be in Neurology. In solution 3, Kwon is in Neurology? Re-check: solution 3 has Kwon: Neurology, which violates rule 4. The only valid assignment here has Jansen in Oncology and Kwon must go to Oncology, leaving Hale in Neurology alone—impossible. Thus C is not viable.
explanations.D: Correct — Hale occupies Neurology in the sole viable configuration under this hypothetical.
explanations.E: Ibarra must be with Gupta in Pediatrics, not Neurology.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

explanations.correct: Oncology already contains Farrell and has only one other slot. If Gupta were in Oncology, Ibarra would also be there (same-department rule), making three in Oncology. Impossible.

questions.questionStem: If Jansen is assigned to Oncology, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hale is not assigned to Oncology.

explanations.correct: If Jansen is in Oncology (with Farrell), Oncology is full. Hale must therefore not be in Oncology (which also satisfies the different-departments rule between Hale and Jansen).
explanations.A: Oncology is full with Farrell and Jansen; Hale cannot be there.
explanations.B: Oncology is full; Kwon cannot be added.
explanations.C: Gupta could be in Neurology (solution 2) or Pediatrics (solution 3). Not forced.
explanations.D: Oncology is full; Ibarra cannot be there.
